preparedCompleteRecord.name: Warding Bond

operational.targets: One willing ally other than yourself, perceived within range and line of effect. Neither participant may already participate in another Warding Bond, as caster or protected ally.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute. In initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; retain that virtual marker through initiative changes, departure or death. Outside initiative, expires 60 seconds after application; entering initiative preserves that absolute deadline. An already-passed start never counts. Ends earlier when concentration ends. Also ends if either participant dies. Reaching 0 HP alone is not a separate ending condition; ordinary Incapacitated/concentration rules still apply.
operational.resolution: Automatic on legal casting. On each eligible positive incoming damage packet to the ally, apply the mandatory post-defense transfer described below; a rounded-zero transfer claims no transfer operation.
operational.effect: The ally gains +1 AC and +1 to saves, subject separately to the strongest applicable flat bonus. After the ally's defenses and legal prevention, before temporary HP, transfer floor(remaining damage / 2) to you and leave the remainder on the ally. Keep the damage type. Your transferred share skips a second mitigation/prevention stage and cannot transfer again; apply your temporary HP, HP, applicable life-state protections, Wounds and concentration consequences normally. The ally retains the hit, failed-save, critical and attached-rider identity; you were not hit and did not fail that save merely because damage transferred.
operational.scaling: None. The rank-2 duplicate grants no upgrade or extra effect.
operational.limitations: Use DAMAGE_SHARING_PLAYTEST.md: one transfer operation per original-recipient damage root, across all owners. A prior pre-mitigation split preempts this transfer; competing positive mandatory post-defense claims are chosen by the original target. The retained ally portion cannot subsequently be transferred again after this split. Complete the current packet's split and life consequences before concentration failure caused by that packet ends the bond; never undo a committed share. One Warding Bond per participating creature across all casters; casting cannot create chains or cycles. Initial range/line of effect are required, but no continuing distance or line-of-effect tether is imposed. This ordinary spell neither consumes nor increases the Paladin class redirection round ledger and grants none of its named healing/resource riders or proc permissions. Unrelated downstream triggers still require their own exact source authorization. Direct HP payments are not damage and cannot be transferred. Known/prepared access, class-level gates, legal components, line of effect, payment before resolution, concentration transitions, Dissonance, Refrain and class cadence follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. No automatic scaling or generic upcast.

NEW: willing ally, conserved mandatory post-defense split, rounding, participation and life endpoints, no continued tether and ordinary-spell/class-engine separation. CONFLICT RULING: source-derived class access is rank 1; duplicate rank-2 block is retained as evidence only.

preparedCompleteRecord.name: Alignment Shield

operational.targets: One willing creature you can perceive with line of effect, including yourself. Actual range is 30 feet when cast through Abjuration rank 1, or 60 feet through Conjuration rank 3; the 60-foot header is the maximum across these modes.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute. In initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; retain that virtual marker through initiative changes, departure or death. Outside initiative, expires 60 seconds after application; entering initiative preserves that absolute deadline. An already-passed start never counts. Ends earlier when concentration ends.
operational.resolution: Automatic after legal casting. For each incoming attack roll, compare the attacker's explicit current canonical alignment with the protected recipient's explicit current canonical alignment.
operational.effect: Grant +2 AC against attack rolls from a creature explicitly opposed to the protected recipient on at least one alignment axis: Lawful versus Chaotic, or Good versus Evil. Neutral is not opposite to any value. An unknown or missing axis supplies no opposition; a known exact opposite on another axis still qualifies. Both class-specific modes use this same bounded bonus.
operational.scaling: None. Only your casting class's listed school/rank mode is available; higher level or extra RP cannot switch modes.
operational.limitations: Never infer alignment from ancestry, faction, reputation, faith, appearance or behavior. The bonus does not identify or announce the attacker's alignment; observers may make ordinary deductions from visible results. The spectral shield creates no equipment, item HP, hand requirement, cover, projectile blocking, saleable object or immunity. It does not affect saving throws or automatically hitting effects. Use only the strongest applicable flat AC bonus. Other concurrent shields retain their own endpoints and concentration dependencies. Known/prepared access, class-level gates, legal components, line of effect, payment before resolution, concentration transitions, Dissonance, Refrain and class cadence follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. No automatic scaling or generic upcast.

NEW CONFLICT RULINGS: Abjuration Instantaneous becomes concentration 1 minute; Conjuration blocks-attacks prose uses +2 AC rather than immunity. NEW: explicit recipient-versus-attacker axis comparison and spectral-only effect.

operational.targets: One fixed 10-foot-radius, 10-foot-high area centered on suitable approximately horizontal immobile ground or surface within range and line of effect. Your casting class selects Abjuration rank 3 or Shaman Conjuration rank 6; rank-6 Conjuration requires both of your canonical alignment axes explicitly recorded before casting.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute. If cast in initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker; preserve that virtual marker through order changes or departure. If cast outside initiative, expires 60 seconds after application; entering initiative preserves that absolute deadline. An already-passed start does not count. Ends earlier if concentration ends.
operational.resolution: Snapshot the caster's actual canonical alignment at application; do not infer it from ancestry, faction, reputation, faith, appearance or conduct. Abjuration rank 3 uses Wisdom saves against your spell DC for opposed entrants. Conjuration rank 6 uses exact matching admission with no save. The snapshot is fixed for this application.
operational.effect: Abjuration rank 3: a creature is opposed if at least one explicitly known axis is exact opposite to the snapshot (Lawful/Chaotic or Good/Evil). Neutral is never opposite; an unknown axis supplies no opposition, and does not erase a known opposite on the other axis. On an opposed creature's attempted entry from outside, roll its Wisdom save before entry, including forced movement, carriage or teleportation. REVIEWED CADENCE CLARIFICATION: record that success or failure for this source character, mode and target until the target's next regular-start marker; the current in-progress start never counts. A success permits entries during that window; failure blocks all non-Falling entry attempts during it without repeat rolls. Same-caster replacement/recasting does not reset this window. Outside initiative, use a fixed 6-second window and preserve its deadline if initiative starts. A failed physical entry stops before the boundary; a failed teleport leaves the creature at its origin without refunding committed teleport costs. Conjuration rank 6: only a creature with both explicit canonical axes exactly matching both snapshotted axes may enter from outside. Unknown is not matching. Nonmatching physical entry, forced movement and carriage stop before entry; a teleport attempt to place a nonmatching creature inside leaves it at origin after costs are committed.
operational.scaling: None. Shaman's preserved Conjuration rank-6 access costs 13 RP before ordinary surcharges; extra RP or character level cannot select another placement.
operational.limitations: Both modes allow existing occupants to remain or leave; once outside, entry restrictions apply. Unsupported ordinary Falling is not arrested, supplies no platform and adds no movement; it can place a creature inside. No AC/save bonus, healing, rest guarantee, resource recovery, attack immunity, concealment, morality compulsion or alignment change. The ward denies entry rather than Actions and does not consume the shared hard-denial ledger. Multiple casters' wards retain independent source permissions and save windows; no single ward's success bypasses another ward. The preserved rank-6 Abjuration aligned-benefits placement has no actual class-access grant and stays unassigned/unavailable; its vague benefits are not imported. Apply SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md for actual class access and repertoire, costs before resolution, components, concentration, Dissonance/Refrain and exact source cadence. No automatic scaling or generic upcast.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action, 60 feet, V/S/F, Abjuration rank-3 opposed-entry Wisdom save and Shaman Conjuration rank-6 same-alignment safe haven. NEW CONFLICT RULINGS: fixed 10-foot-radius/height and concentration 1 minute replace Instantaneous metadata; actual modes stay separate, unassigned rank-6 Abjuration benefits remain blocked. NEW: snapshots, entry/teleport/Falling handling and exact two-axis Conjuration matching. Save-window/recast and rank-6 snapshot-validity completions are jointly reviewed provisional rules.

operational.targets: One perceptible ongoing magical effect with a discrete spatial origin/area within range and line of effect, created by you or explicitly permitted for anchoring by its current source owner/controller. It cannot be Resonance Anchor, an effect permanently attached to a creature/carried object, or an effect currently dependent on your own existing concentration.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute. If cast in initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker; preserve that virtual marker through order changes or departure. If cast outside initiative, expires 60 seconds after application; entering initiative preserves that absolute deadline. An already-passed start does not count. Ends earlier if concentration ends. Also ends when the anchored target effect ends.
operational.resolution: Automatic after legal casting. Check the own-concentration exclusion before committing this cast: it forbids targeting an effect that beginning Anchor would itself end.
operational.effect: Fix the selected effect's spatial origin in its current position; a movable/recenterable zone loses that relocation permission while anchored. Ordinary dispelling cannot end the target, including otherwise eligible Dispel Minor, Dispel Resonance, Dispel Magic (Lesser) or Dispel Magic. Anchor itself remains normally dispellable at its own actual rank. REVIEWED CLARIFICATION: anchoring fixes location, not the target's unrelated source-authorized evolution of radius, shape or nonspatial effects; it neither freezes nor manufactures those source changes.
operational.scaling: None.
operational.limitations: Cannot target itself or another Resonance Anchor. No duration extension, replacement of the target's concentration, use/cost reset, revival, restored pulse, frozen expiry or retroactive Counterspell protection. The target can still end by its own concentration, duration, destruction, source conditions, special removal or explicit anchor-bypassing effect. Its original owner/controller can still exercise a printed ending permission. Another caster's anchored concentration spell still requires that caster's concentration. No class engine or full Time Loop implementation is granted. Apply SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md for actual class access and repertoire, costs before resolution, components, concentration, Dissonance/Refrain and exact source cadence. No automatic scaling or generic upcast.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action, 60 feet, V/S/F, fixing a magical effect and preventing ordinary dispel. NEW CONFLICT RULING: concentration 1 minute replaces Instantaneous metadata. NEW: spatial eligibility/controller permission, own-concentration exclusion, Anchor's removability and no mutual anchoring. Location remains fixed while otherwise source-authorized size/shape evolution continues.

preparedCompleteRecord.name: Counterspell

operational.activation: Reaction — when another creature you can perceive within range and line of effect begins casting a spell, after its casting costs and cadence are committed but before its effect resolves
operational.targets: One pending spell cast by the triggering creature. The spell needs an actual recorded rank; the Director may know that rank without revealing it to you.
operational.duration: Instantaneous
operational.resolution: make a spellcasting-ability check using the actual ability for the class through which you cast Counterspell, adding PB once, against DC 10 + twice the triggering spell's actual rank (rank 0 contributes 0). Use CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md's fixed-DC task degrees and natural shifts: at least DC+10 Critical Success, at least DC Success, at most DC-10 Critical Failure, otherwise Failure; natural 20 improves one degree and natural 1 worsens one. Collapse both upper degrees to success and both lower degrees to failure; invent no additional critical effect. This is not a spell attack or saving throw.
operational.effect: Success negates the selected pending spell after its costs were committed; failure lets it continue. Every interruptible cast first commits its RP/material/other costs, components, concentration transition, Dissonance/Refrain and exact beginning/casting hooks once, then opens the interruption window. A surviving cast later resolves its effect and outcome-dependent hooks. Negation gives no refund, no successful-effect trigger and no restoration of old concentration. Counterspell is itself a spell and can be countered. Resolve nested counters last-in, first-out; if a counter is negated, the earlier pending spell resumes without paying or casting again. Resuming a parent never rewrites the later nested cast's Refrain/Dissonance history.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic success against lower ranks and no generic upcast.
operational.limitations: One attempt per creature against a particular pending cast, shared across ordinary, Wizard, Mage and other same-named Counterspell sources. An exact source that expressly grants an additional Counterspell attempt against the same pending cast overrides this default; merely granting another Reaction does not. After a failed attempt another eligible creature may react; once negated, the spell supplies no further interruption trigger. All reactions need their own legal remaining resource, components, range and current source permissions. Attempting does not reveal spell identity/rank; never treat an unassigned rank as 0 or estimate it from RP. Ready opens its cast-interruption window at preparation, not release. Countering is not whole-Action/turn hard denial and does not spend that ledger. Ordinary Counterspell requires ordinary repertoire/class access and rank-3 cost; Wizard/Mage same-named class cards keep their own separate acquisition, printed costs, ranks, recharge and text. Apply SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md for actual class access and repertoire, costs before resolution, components, concentration, Dissonance/Refrain and exact source cadence. No automatic scaling or generic upcast.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: both Abjuration/Universal rank-3 placements, Reaction, 60 feet, V/S/F and instantaneous interruption. NEW: actual casting ability+PB against DC 10+2*rank, one attempt per pending cast, hidden-rank handling and nested timing. REVIEWED SOURCE CORRECTION: the earlier binary-check proposal is superseded by the existing Core fixed-DC task rule, with natural shifts and collapsed success/failure outcomes. Exact source permission may override the shared attempt limit; another Reaction alone cannot.
operational.implementationStatus: REVIEWED authored operational-playtest manuscript; runtime and balance validation pending

preparedCompleteRecord.name: Summon Fire Pet

operational.targets: One unoccupied space you can perceive within range; summons one Small fire elemental companion
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
operational.resolution: No initial save or attack. The summoned pet uses your spell attack bonus for its commanded melee attack.
operational.effect: Summon a Small fire elemental with AC 13, 10 HP, Speed 30 feet, and a melee fire attack with 5-foot reach using your spell attack bonus. On hit it deals 1d8 fire damage. It acts immediately after you. On your Bonus Action command it may move and either make its one melee attack or take another basic non-damaging action; without a command it may move and Dodge. Its saving throw bonus is your PB; ability checks use +0 unless its profile explicitly supplies another bonus. It has no innate resistances or immunities beyond this printed profile.
operational.scaling: None. Damage dice, target count, range and duration do not automatically increase with character or class level.
operational.limitations: You may have only one Summon Fire Pet from this spell at a time. It shares the owner's global companion command budget and one damaging companion action per round across all companions. It has no independent resource generation, class features, loot, corpse, death trigger, free healing, or autonomous attack. At 0 HP or when concentration ends it disappears. Recasting replaces the prior pet. Ranked casting causes normal Dissonance and Refrain.
operational.designNotes: Core V2 blocks and catalog summaries are preserved alongside this card. Components use the existing class focus where Core says F or M/F; this focus interpretation is provisional. Exact target eligibility, duration endpoints, saves where absent, concentration where unclear and anti-loop limits are provisional integration decisions.
operational.previousDraftDesignNotes: NEW provisional speed, attack bonus, command economy, concentration, and companion restrictions. Source-specific AC 13, HP 10, Small size, and 1d8 fire melee override generic companion statistics.

preparedCompleteRecord.name: Summon Air Pet

operational.targets: One unoccupied space you can perceive within range.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute. If applied in initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; preserve that virtual phase through initiative changes, absence or death. Outside initiative, expires 60 seconds after application; retain that absolute deadline on entering initiative. An already-passed start never counts. Ends earlier if concentration ends or the pet reaches 0 HP.
operational.resolution: No initial roll. On a legal damaging command the pet takes one offensive action containing two separate melee spell attacks, using your actual casting-class spell attack bonus, reach 5 feet. Each hit deals 1d6 slashing damage with no ability damage modifier; resolve ordinary attack/critical/defense rules separately.
operational.effect: Summon one Small air elemental with AC 15, HP 20, walking Speed 30 feet, saves equal to owner PB, other checks +0, ordinary sight/hearing, and a body mass of 20 pounds. It understands your spoken commands but has no speaking language or telepathy. It acts immediately after you. While within 60 feet and able to perceive your command, your Bonus Action commands movement plus its two-attack offensive action or one basic legal nondamaging action. Both attacks may target one creature or separate legal creatures within reach at each attack. Any movement between attacks uses its normal available movement, not extra movement.
operational.scaling: Only the expressly printed owner PB saves and actual spell attack bonus change with the caster. AC15, HP20, two attacks and 1d6 damage remain fixed; no S-dice progression.
operational.limitations: The printed two attacks are a specific exception to the ordinary one-attack companion profile, not two Actions or two commands. Declaring this offensive action consumes the owner-wide one damaging companion action for that numbered round, including if attacks miss or the second attack cannot occur; no other companion receives offense from the remaining portion. Without a command it may defensively move and Dodge, with no autonomous attacks. It shares the owner-wide Bonus Action companion command budget. Air grants no flight, hover, gaseous passage, resistance, immunity, special senses or borrowed monster statistics. It grants no hands/tool operation, cargo carriage, free Help advantage, independent spellcasting, corpse, loot, resource/death triggers, free resummoning or autonomous opportunity attack. One pet per caster; at 0 HP or concentration end it vanishes. Recasting pays a new cast. Carrying this pet uses its actual printed mass and the body/carrying guide; it creates no permanent material. A successful new application owns its own endpoint; stale cleanup of a prior application cannot end its replacement. A countered cast creates no replacement. Starting concentration still ends the caster's incompatible prior concentration before interruption. Known/prepared access, actual class rank/level, V/S/F components, line of effect, costs, concentration transitions, Dissonance/Refrain, class hooks and interruption follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Total cover blocks originating line of effect and direct targeting. No generic upcast or unstated scaling.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action/30 feet/V/S/F/concentration 1 minute, AC15/HP20 and two 1d6 slashing attacks. NEW: Small/walking30/ordinary senses, command/profile details and the bounded two-attacks-in-one-action exception consuming all owner companion offense. Exact-card completion adds 20-pound body mass and no ungranted hands/cargo capacity. AC, HP and damage do not scale; PB/actual spell attack follow the printed owner interface.
operational.implementationStatus: REVIEWED authored operational-playtest manuscript; runtime, CR certification and numerical balance pending

preparedCompleteRecord.name: Faction Portal

operational.targets: One legal open local entrance space you perceive within 60 feet and line of effect, on suitable ground. Choose one exact canonical factionId with a recorded current reputation score above 0 and one specific known headquarters of that faction.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute. In initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; preserve the virtual phase through initiative changes, absence, death and planar travel. Outside initiative, expires 60 seconds after application, retaining that absolute deadline when entering initiative. An already-passed start does not count. Ends earlier if concentration ends.
operational.resolution: No roll. On successful casting create one visible, fixed, one-way doorway 5 feet wide and8 feet high. The destination is a known established public/default receiving point for the chosen headquarters, or, absent such a point, one specific known ordinary primary entrance/foyer. Identify it from personal experience or reliable public information; no existing portal infrastructure is needed. It may be on the same or another plane. Recheck each actual crossing against legal arrival space and exact teleport/planar blockers; failure leaves the crossing creature and belongings at the local entrance, with no split or deletion.
operational.effect:
Any creature that physically fits the entrance under ordinary anatomy/squeezing rules may use it; passengers need no positive reputation or faction membership. Entering costs 5 feet of ordinary movement, subject to ordinary movement-cost adjustments, and atomically transports that creature and its legally carried belongings to a legal unoccupied space at or adjacent to the chosen receiving point. Ordinary carried creatures may accompany it only within the carrier's actual anatomy, pound and Load capacity and with room for the whole arriving group; this does not create willing-target immunity against being actually carried. Choose the receiving point when casting and keep it fixed. At each crossing use the nearest legal space at/adjacent to that point that fits the whole group, with a fixed neutral board order for ties, never a tactical remote choice or search through barriers. If none exists, the crossing fails and the attempted movement remains spent. Ordinary approach movement can provoke opportunity attacks; the teleport transition itself cannot. Items carried through remain the same items with actual ownership, contents, conditions and provenance. Loose unattended objects do not independently activate transit: a creature must physically carry or legally handle them as part of its own crossing; thrown projectiles, remote pushes and spells cannot deliver goods through by themselves.

The doorway is opaque to sight and sound and supplies no line of effect through it. Attacks, spells, areas, projectiles and remote sensing do not pass. There is no exit doorway or automatic return route. Complete a currently resolving legal crossing atomically before closing/suppressing the doorway; expiry never bisects a body or cargo. Later crossings require the still-active doorway. Suppression makes it unusable without pausing its endpoint. It has no physical HP, support or barrier body; when inactive there is no active transit surface. One portal per caster; a successful replacement closes the old one. Current positive reputation is checked as a creation gate at cast start and resolution, not a continuing passenger credential; a later standing change does not itself close a created portal.
operational.scaling: None.
operational.limitations: Use the actual canonical reputation record: positive means above 0, normally+1 through+3 under REPUTATION.md; missing/0/negative standing fails the gate. This card does not replace that scale with the historical Gameplay Loop's -5..+5 scale. No faction membership, Seal invocation permission, headquarters infrastructure or automatic entry authorization is added. If there are several HQs, select exactly one known site; no hidden vault, secret room, unknown HQ, location search or knowledge report. The far endpoint needs no originating line of sight/effect and has no geographic range ceiling, but actual wards and legal placement still apply. A headquarters that ceases to exist or belong to the faction cannot receive new crossings; a purely clerical name change does not move the chosen physical point. Failed crossings reveal no cause beyond failure, although ordinary observers may draw inferences. The spell can bypass a geographic route leg and deliver people to Haven when that actual HQ is there. It never automatically completes Extraction, advances or resets the Opening clock, settles cargo claims, removes contamination, changes ownership/reputation, grants credentials, ignores guards/laws/taxes or refunds cast costs. No free actions, additional capacity, object duplication or attacker path across planes. A successful replacement has its own endpoint; stale cleanup cannot end the new application. A countered cast creates no replacement, although its concentration transition has already occurred. Actual class access, rank, preparation, V/S/F components, casting costs, Dissonance/Refrain, class hooks, concentration transitions and counter windows follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Costs and beginning hooks commit before interruption, with no refunds or restoration of prior concentration. Direct target selection and local creation require the printed line of effect; expressly remote teleport destinations use their own printed rules. No generic upcast or unstated scaling.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action/60 feet/V,S,F, doorway to a faction headquarters with positive reputation, actual planar travel supported by Planar tag. CONFLICT RULING: Core Instantaneous metadata becomes NEW 1 minute concentration for a usable doorway. NEW: known ordinary receiving-site procedure, fixed one-way 5 x 8 ft entrance, local 5 foot movement cost, whole-group atomic arrival, opaque transport-only interface, any-passenger use, no later reputation tether and exact destination legality. Canon positive predicate is retained without silently changing the reputation scale; route bypass remains possible while actual settlement procedures persist.

preparedCompleteRecord.name: Resonance Well

operational.targets: One fixed point you can perceive within range and line of effect for a nonphysical pool of resonance.
operational.duration: If applied in initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; preserve that virtual phase through initiative changes, absence or death. Outside initiative, expires 60 seconds after application; retain that absolute deadline on entering initiative. An already-passed start never counts. Ends earlier if the spell is ended or a later successful allowed application replaces it.
operational.resolution: Before activation/payment confirm the caster's unused character-wide Resonance Well creation use. Spend it at legal cast start before the Counterspell window. On successful resolution roll 1d4 exactly once to establish the total RP reserve. This amount belongs to the entire Well, not each recipient.
operational.effect: One creation use per character across classes/copies refreshes only at that character's actual beneficial completed long rest. A countered cast spends the use and creates no Well. A creature with an actual RP pool, including the caster, can spend an Action within 5 feet and line of effect to draw. Verify its unused character-wide Resonance Well receipt use since its own last beneficial completed long rest and a positive remaining reserve. At draw start choose a positive amount no greater than that reserve, spend the recipient use and Action, and subtract that amount immediately. At resolution restore the chosen amount, capped at actual RP maximum. Over-cap recovery is wasted; a full recipient can deliberately spend a positive draw and recover 0. Zero draw is illegal. A preventing interrupt refunds nothing.
operational.scaling: None.
operational.limitations: One Well per caster. Receipt use is shared across all Wells/casters/classes and refreshes only at the recipient's own beneficial long rest; creation and receipt are separate records, including when caster draws from their own Well. Kindle and Mod Rod keep their separate named ledgers: Well neither resets nor shares them. At reserve 0 the Well is inert until its endpoint. Re-entry, suppression, replacement, dispelling, copying or recovery prevention never rerolls/refills the reserve or restores spent uses. Suppression prevents drawing while applicable and does not pause duration; if drawing was already committed, a subsequent actual prevention leaves its amount/use spent. This fixed nonphysical resonance cannot be carried as water, harvested, sold, used as Supply, drawn at range or treated as a pooled RP maximum. It provides no physical support, hazard or damage despite the historical Damage tag. A successful new application owns its own endpoint; stale cleanup of a prior application cannot end its replacement. A countered cast creates no replacement. Starting concentration still ends the caster's incompatible prior concentration before interruption. Known/prepared access, actual class rank/level, V/S/F components, line of effect, costs, concentration transitions, Dissonance/Refrain, class hooks and interruption follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Total cover blocks originating line of effect and direct targeting. No generic upcast or unstated scaling.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action/30 feet/V/S/F and a pool from which allies draw 1d4 RP. CONFLICT RULING: finite 1-minute nonconcentration pool replaces Instantaneous metadata; Damage tag grants no unprinted damage. NEW: one rolled total reserve, explicit Action/5-foot draw, caster inclusion, positive committed withdrawals and distinct creation/receipt limits per beneficial long rest. Source supplied no daily limit; both anti-farm limits are explicitly provisional additions, not recovered canon.

operational.targets: One fixed point or nonliving surface you perceive within range and line of effect. Choose an exact canonical factionId whose ordinary name/symbol you know; no reputation, membership or Faction Seal invocation gate is added.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute. If applied in initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; preserve that virtual phase through initiative changes, absence or death. Outside initiative, expires 60 seconds after application; retain that absolute deadline on entering initiative. An already-passed start never counts. Ends earlier if concentration ends.
operational.resolution: Automatic display. At each saving throw, the Director evaluates actual current membership and location/line of effect for the creature making the save; no roll or magical membership report is supplied by creation.
operational.effect: Create a visible, nonphysical emblem at most 2 feet across. Its aura is a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on the emblem. A creature with an explicit actual membership record for that faction gains +1 to saving throws while within the aura and line of effect to it. This includes the caster only if actually eligible. Leaving the area or losing membership removes eligibility; entering or gaining membership permits it. A display placed on a movable nonliving object moves with that object; a free-standing point remains fixed. It emits no light, uses ordinary visibility, and needs no separate action to maintain the aura.
operational.scaling: None.
operational.limitations: One Greater Emblem per caster; successful recasting replaces the old display. The strongest applicable same-stat flat bonus applies: overlapping emblems, including different factions, never add multiple +1 bonuses to one save. Neutral/positive reputation alone is not actual membership, and missing membership is not presumed. The effect does not reveal membership, identity, reputation, rank, credentials, alignment, intent or hidden faction data. Director-held actual records can establish eligibility without revealing them; observers may draw ordinary deductions from events. No authority, allegiance, persuasion, prices, RP discounts, immunity, healing, resource gain, guaranteed belief, physical token or permanent crafting symbol is supplied. A successful new application owns its own endpoint; stale cleanup of a prior application cannot end its replacement. A countered cast creates no replacement. Starting concentration still ends the caster's incompatible prior concentration before interruption. Known/prepared access, actual class rank/level, V/S/F components, line of effect, costs, concentration transitions, Dissonance/Refrain, class hooks and interruption follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Total cover blocks originating line of effect and direct targeting. No generic upcast or unstated scaling.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action/30 feet/V/S/F and a faction symbol granting benefits to actual members. NEW: precisely +1 saves, 10-foot spherical aura, 2-foot display, 1-minute concentration, known ordinary symbol/name, actual membership predicate and one-caster cap. The source gives no positive-reputation gate, so none is imported. Exact-card completion follows the reviewed ordinary emblem's fixed-point versus surface-following distinction; the aura follows only the actual emblem.

operational.targets: One creature you perceive within30feet and line of effect. No requirement that its alignment be known; hidden canonical axes are resolved after paid casting.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to1minute. In initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; an already-passed start never counts. Outside initiative, expires after 60 elapsed seconds. Retain the original virtual phase or absolute deadline through initiative changes, absence and planar travel; moving between timing modes does not reset it.
operational.resolution: The target makes a Wisdom save. Success: no new overlay. Failure: snapshot your actual current alignment orientation. For each axis defined both for you and for the target, compute one step toward your snapshotted value along Lawful–Neutral–Chaotic and Good–Neutral–Evil. Compute the target baseline without any previous Alignment Suggestion overlay on that target, retaining all independent actual alignment effects/records. An already matching or undefined axis gains no changed-value overlay. If at least one axis changes, replace the prior same-spell overlay with the new recorded axis values/deadline. A failed-save cast that changes no defined axis creates no new overlay and does not itself replace a valid older one; mandatory concentration transitions remain independent.
operational.effect: The changed values are the target’s actual effective canonical alignment for rules that query those axes during the overlay, including real alignment-gated spells/items. Example: baseline Chaotic Evil targeted by a Lawful Good caster becomes Neutral Neutral; one such overlay never jumps two steps. Its values remain fixed until expiry/removal/replacement and do not recompute every time another underlying record changes. Unchanged/unoverlaid axes follow their actual underlying records. An independent effect such as Corrupted can change underlying alignment while this spell persists; that change remains and is exposed when the applicable overlay ends. One Alignment Suggestion overlay per target across casters; recasting cannot use its old overlay as a staircase for another same-spell step.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in range, targets, duration, magnitude or uses.
operational.limitations: The spell grants no automatic knowledge of either character’s axes, including whether a value changed. Actual information protections still govern observations. It never compels matching behavior, belief, confession, loyalty, PvP, personality or oathbreaking; conduct clauses still judge actual conduct. Ending removes only this overlay, without restoring an old alignment snapshot, deleting independent changes or reviving a replaced overlay. Caster orientation is fixed at application, not tracked through later caster changes. Ward tag creates no ward. More specific alignment-changing effects retain their actual interaction rules; this card does not invent a general priority engine for every unrelated overlay. Actual class access/repertoire, costs, components, Dissonance/Refrain, concentration transitions and cast/counter order follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Pay a legal cast before effect resolution; failure/countering refunds nothing and restores no displaced concentration. V is audible, S requires the ordinary usable hand, and F is the normal class focus. Saves use the actual casting class's spell DC and binary save rules. Creature type alone supplies no mental immunity; Charmed-only immunity does not block effects that never impose Charmed. Actual broader defenses retain their written scope. No automatic scaling, generic upcast or free identification of hidden eligibility.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action/30feet/V,S,M/F as focus, WIS, concentration minute and actual push toward caster alignment. NEW: temporary canonical one-step overlay on both eligible axes. Exact-review proposals: compute without previous same-spell overlay to prevent recast ratcheting, overlay only genuinely changed axes, fixed values, and no new application when no defined axis changes; independent base changes survive ending.

operational.targets: Declare an ordered list of distinct creatures you perceive within 30 feet and line of effect before hidden HP or defense resolution. A creature appears at most once in this cast’s list.
operational.duration: Independent Sleep-caused Unconscious on each affected creature, up to1minute, no concentration. In initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; an already-passed start never counts. Outside initiative, expires after 60 elapsed seconds. Retain the original virtual phase or absolute deadline through initiative changes, absence and planar travel; moving between timing modes does not reset it.
operational.resolution: No saving throw. After casting commits and survives interruption, start one fixed budget of24. In declared order, each creature costs max(1, its current ordinary HP) at this resolution; temporary HP are ignored. If that cost exceeds the remaining budget, stop without attempting that creature or later entries. Otherwise deduct that cost before testing defenses/guard and attempt the Unconscious application. An attempted immune, protected or hard-guard-blocked creature still spends its HP cost. Budget/allocation/hidden defenses receive no special diagnostic disclosure; ordinary visible results remain observable.
operational.effect: A successful application imposes the actual Unconscious condition, including its inherited Incapacitated, awareness, movement, speech, held-item, Prone, save and attack consequences subject to actual component immunities. Each target uses its own shared source-character/target hard-control history. A0HP creature costs1 and retains its separate0HP state and Unconscious source. End a Sleep application when its target receives a positive damage packet after defenses and before temporary HP, when another creature within physical reach spends an Action rousing it, on its deadline, or through an applicable removal rule. Physical rousing by that Action ends all applications of this ordinary Sleep spell on that creature, but does not cure unrelated Unconscious causes. All Sleep applications independently see a qualifying damage event. The waking damage attack resolves using the conditions present for its roll/hit, then the damage event ends Sleep; no retroactive critical/hit reversal.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in range, targets, duration, magnitude or uses.
operational.limitations: A fully prevented zero packet does not wake by damage; positive packet can wake even if an HP floor prevents actual numeric HP loss. No self-awakening while Unconscious, automatic stabilization, healing, death-save reset or removal of other causes. No rolled HP budget, creature-type sleep immunity or concentration is imported. Recasts pay again and cannot refresh the shared guard; an unsuccessful new application leaves old valid sources intact. Suppression clocks continue and never replay the original drop/Prone event when suppression ends. Hard whole-Action/turn components use the existing combined source-character/target/encounter allowance across class features, spells and companions. A blocked hard component gains no invented fallback; independent printed components retain their own defense checks. A successfully established hard component claims the allowance once, not again each turn; ending, dispelling, replacing or suppressing it does not refund the encounter history. Actual boss/control immunities remain effective. Actual class access/repertoire, costs, components, Dissonance/Refrain, concentration transitions and cast/counter order follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Pay a legal cast before effect resolution; failure/countering refunds nothing and restores no displaced concentration. V is audible, S requires the ordinary usable hand, and F is the normal class focus. Saves use the actual casting class's spell DC and binary save rules. Creature type alone supplies no mental immunity; Charmed-only immunity does not block effects that never impose Charmed. Actual broader defenses retain their written scope. No automatic scaling, generic upcast or free identification of hidden eligibility.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action/30feet/V,S,F, fixed24HP and explicitly no save. NEW: ordered current-HP/minimum1 budgeting, finite minute, waking and helper Action. Exact completion: helper rousing ends this named spell’s Sleep applications, not every cause of Unconscious; damage timing preserves an already determined hit/critical.

currentSourceCatalogRecord.name: Hypnotic Pattern

operational.targets: Choose a point you perceive with line of effect: within 60 feet for actual Enchantment casting access, or within 30 feet for actual Illusion casting access. Center a fixed 30-foot cube on that point, extending 15 feet along each axis. At resolution snapshot every creature physically in the cube with line of effect from its center that can actually see the pattern, including allies and yourself; no selective omission. The numeric range field records the maximum mode, not permission for Illusion to use 60 feet.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to one minute, with independent damage/rousing endings per affected creature. In initiative, the maximum ends at the caster's tenth future regular-turn START after application, excluding any start already underway/passed. If begun outside initiative, the maximum is 60 elapsed seconds. Preserve the original virtual marker/absolute deadline through initiative changes, extra turns, absence and planar travel; no timing-mode change resets it.
operational.resolution: Use the actual class’s school and rank-3/5-RP access. Enchantment access belongs to Bard, Crimson Agent, Mirrorsage, Thief, Wizard and Paladin at their preserved levels; Monk’s actual mode is Illusion. Each eligible creature makes a Wisdom save. Success: no new components. Failure independently attempts Core Charmed toward you and actual Incapacitated. Charmed immunity blocks only Charmed; the Incapacitated component has its own defenses and shared hard-control allowance. A blocked hard component can leave independently legal Charmed. Apply the NEW spell-specific atomic initial batch in the shared rank-three manuscript: snapshot eligibility, resolve saves and legal components, apply every target’s components/immediate consequences, then process queued teardown of this Pattern if your own Incapacitated ended its concentration. Do not abort later targets because of iteration order.
operational.effect: Actual Charmed and Incapacitated retain their separate printed effects. Incapacitated ends applicable existing concentration and denies its ordinary covered action types; it does not inherently set Speed to 0. If self-Incapacitated ends your Pattern, other targets still receive that same initial batch and its real immediate consequences before this cast’s maintained components are removed. The visible lights remain in the fixed cube while concentration lasts but grant no general illumination, concealment or sight through obscurity. This is an initial snapshot: later entrants or initially ineligible creatures do not receive new applications. Later loss of sight does not end an existing application. End both still-present components from this cast on a creature when it receives positive post-defense/pre-temp-HP damage, or when another creature within physical reach uses an Action to rouse one selected Pattern application. Damage resolution preserves already-established hit/critical outcomes. No repeat saves.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in range, targets, duration, magnitude or uses.
operational.limitations: A fully prevented zero damage packet does not wake; a positive packet can wake even when temporary HP or an HP floor prevents ordinary HP loss. Rousing ends one actual cast’s application only, not every Pattern or unrelated condition source. If the helper cannot distinguish several Pattern applications, select one by stable application order without disclosing hidden source metadata. Recasts create independent sources subject to actual concentration transitions and each new hard-component check; an exact multiple-concentration feature does not convert them into refreshes. A Charmed-only remnant receives no invented repeat save. No unaware, Unconscious, Prone, Speed 0 or forced item drop is added. Ordinary darkness/obscurity can prevent initial actual sight even though the pattern itself is visible. Hard whole-Action/turn components share the combined source-character/target/encounter allowance across class features, spells and companions. Successful establishment claims it once, not per affected turn. Ending, replacing, dispelling or suppressing a hard component never refunds the history. A blocked hard component gains no invented fallback; independently printed components retain their actual defenses. Initial prevention leaves no deferred hard application. Later suppression of an established component preserves its clock and spent history. Actual boss/control immunities remain effective. The accompanying ENCHANTMENT_RANK3_INTEGRATION_PLAYTEST.md supplies the expressly bound timing/component procedure; it grants no extra turn, action, hidden information or source access. Actual class access/repertoire, legal action/components/RP, concentration transitions, Dissonance/Refrain and paid cast/counter order follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. A legal cast pays before hidden eligibility/effect resolution; failure or countering refunds nothing and restores no displaced concentration. V is audible, S needs the ordinary usable hand, and F is the normal class focus. Saves use the actual casting class's spell DC and binary-save rules. Hidden eligibility supplies no free diagnostic. Creature type alone supplies no mental immunity; Charmed-only immunity has only its actual condition scope. No generic upcast, extra action budget or resource generation.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: both schools/rank-3/5-RP class access, Action/V/S/F, Enchantment range 60 and Illusion range 30, concentration minute, Charmed/Incapacitated; Illusion supplies 30-foot cube and WIS. NEW: harmonized cube/save for Enchantment, perceived center/center-LoE/sight snapshot, separate components, waking, and spell-specific atomic self-concentration cleanup. No unprinted Speed 0 or entry aura is imported.

# Spell integration rules — provisional v0.1

Use this document with the [shared class rules](CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md), the class's own engine and the [spell packet](SPELL_PLAYTEST_STARTER.md). This is a staged development layer, not an approved-book replacement or a live companion update.

## What owns each decision

| Decision | Source used for this packet |
|---|---|
| Spell identity, every school placement and per-class rank/access | Preserved `src/data/spells.js`; do not collapse different class ranks into one global rank. |
| Common RP prices and additional spell evidence | Core Systems Known Descent V2. Its spell blocks are retained with the catalog summaries. |
| Class identity, engine, spellbook/preparation and cadence exceptions | The current class playtest packet. |
| Generic Dissonance/Refrain, action limits and core conditions | Shared class playtest rules; source Core conditions remain unchanged. |
| Missing targeting, exact endpoints, concentration ambiguities and exploit limits | Explicitly provisional decisions on each spell card. |

The approved Core V2 source has 936 spell blocks. The companion catalog has 848 unique IDs with 936 school placements, but leaves four metadata fields unspecified. These are different views of the source, not evidence that all casting details were absent. Core's generic “Automatic or opposed as described” does not supply a concrete save or targeting rule.

Eleven possible renamed entries remain comparative evidence in the register. Harmonic Bulwark's catalog summary says 5 temporary HP per RP while the possible historical Mana Shield entry says 2; its [individual transformation and buffer review](TRANSFORMATION_SPELL_PLAYTEST.md) now supplies the operational decision. Both source variants remain preserved. Other unresolved aliases stay pending their own review; matching names never silently merge effects.

Resonance Kindle now has [exact manuscript approval](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CONJURATION_CANTRIP_EXACT_REVIEW.md): Action/Self/V/S, recover 1 RP only when this spell reaches resolution. Its one character-wide use is spent at legal cast start and refreshes only on a beneficial completed long rest. The comparative Mana Kindle block remains separately preserved; its broader wording does not trigger recovery from other cantrips and its historical range grants no remote recipient. The [Conjuration cantrip status](CONJURATION_CANTRIP_REVIEW_STATUS.json) records this bounded decision and the other eleven approved cards.

## Select a spell

1. Choose the class through which you are learning/casting it. Check that class's school access and minimum **class** level on the card.
2. Use that class's spell rank and Core V2 cost. A different eligible class may receive the same spell at a different rank and level.
3. Record it in your allowed known, prepared or spellbook choices. An eligible catalog entry is not an automatic grant. Wizard and Druid keep their explicit preparation systems; fallback counts apply only where the class has no more specific rule.
4. Select only a spell marked `operational-playtest-draft` in this packet, or an operational spell expressly supplied by a class card. Other records stay visible in the unfinished queue.
5. A class card and an ordinary spell with the same name remain separate records with separate acquisition and costs. Knowing one does not grant the other. Oath spells, Matrix techniques and similar class spells use their own card.

Oracle uses RC and its Mystery/Curse system. Soldier and Warrior have no general Weave access. Dragoon first gains ordinary magic at class 3; Paladin at class 2. Sufficient RP, total character level, a class feature with the same name, or a borrowed spellbook cannot bypass a gate.

## Resolve a cast at the table

1. Verify the available Action/Bonus Action/Reaction, its exact trigger, components, targets, range and line of effect. No legal target means no activation or payment. A target in an area still needs the card's eligibility. Total cover blocks direct targeting unless expressly overridden.
2. Choose a spell from your actual repertoire. Determine its class-specific rank and RP cost: rank 0–9 costs **0/2/3/5/7/10/13/17/21/26**. Add explicitly printed extra costs; Resonance Shield adds 1 RP even when the caster receives it as a cantrip. Generic Overcast is excluded.
3. Read Dissonance **before** casting. Limit = max(4, 2 + PB + max(0, casting modifier)). At limit/limit+3/limit+6, ranked spells cost +1/+2/+3 RP. At limit+6 ordinary rank-1+ casting is blocked. Cantrips have no strain surcharge but still build Refrain. An expressly granted traumatic-casting exception pays the cost and its printed trauma; it grants neither rank nor repertoire access.
4. Commit the legal cast's RP, materials and other printed costs before any attack/save or interruption. Perform its components and establish concentration if required, ending incompatible prior concentration. An ordinary missed, saved-against or countered legal cast refunds nothing and never restores displaced concentration.
5. At this cast's beginning, apply ordinary Dissonance and Refrain once: 0 base for rank 0, 1 for ranks 1–5, 2 for ranks 6–9; consecutive same-named casts add Refrain +1/+2/+3, capped at +3. First cast or a different name adds +0. Apply the class's exact protected reduction, routing or vent and any hook whose printed trigger is beginning/casting. Weapon or idle turns do not reset the previous name/Refrain unless the class expressly says so. This chronological commitment occurs before the Counterspell window; a later Reaction cast updates its own history, and resuming the earlier cast does not update that history again.
6. Open legal cast-interruption Reactions, resolving nested counters last-in, first-out. A surviving cast then resolves its effect: spell attacks are d20 + PB + the actual casting ability modifier; save DC is 8 + PB + that modifier. Use the exact card's hit/failure/success results and ordinary damage/conditions. Outcome-dependent class hooks occur only at their printed timing and with the required actual result. No automatic cantrip scaling applies. A negated spell grants no success/hit/damage effect merely because its casting cost was paid.
7. Record concentration, exact expiration, per-rest use, summon and companion command obligations. A second spell cannot supply an ungranted Action, duplicate concentration or resource reset. A readied spell commits this casting sequence at preparation; release has no second cast, cost, cadence update or Counterspell window.

Countering requires an actual operational spell or class card, its repertoire/access and a legal remaining Reaction. The ordinary Counterspell is now reviewed; it is separate from the Mage and Wizard class cards. Dispel Minor, Dispel Resonance, Dispel Magic (Lesser) and Dispel Magic use their exact individual scopes. Rank-limited dispels inspect the original generating cast's spell rank, not RP cost or the dispeller's rank. Higher and unassigned source variants retain their own unfinished status.

## Counterspell checks and interruption

The [exact notebook review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ABJURATION_RANK2_3_EXACT_REVIEW.md) confirms this authored timing interface and corrects the earlier binary-check proposal using the existing [Core roll rules](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md). This is a tabletop procedure; the pricing helper does not implement nested reactions.

Ordinary Counterspell uses its casting class's actual spellcasting ability + PB against **DC 10 + twice the triggering spell's actual rank**. The class Wizard/Mage cards retain their printed Intelligence + PB check and their own acquisition, cost, rank and recharge. Apply the existing fixed-DC task degrees and natural shifts, then collapse Critical Success/Success to success and Failure/Critical Failure to failure. No extra critical counter effect is invented. It is neither a spell attack nor a saving throw.

| Natural d20 + modifier | DC | Existing task result | Counter result |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 20 + 0 | 22 | Failure improves to Success | Success |
| 1 + 9 | 10 | Success worsens to Failure | Failure |
| 1 + 20 | 10 | Critical Success worsens to Success | Success |

The target must be an actual pending spell with a recorded rank. The Director may use hidden source data without revealing the spell's identity/rank; attempting grants no free identification. An unassigned rank is not automatically zero. A source-defined technique is not counterable merely because it spends RP or resembles magic.

A creature normally attempts Counterspell once against a particular pending cast, across its ordinary and same-named class sources. Another Reaction alone does not supply another attempt. An exact source expressly granting an additional attempt against that same cast overrides the default. After failure, another eligible creature may react; after negation there is no further trigger. Counterspell is itself a spell and can be countered. Resolve nested counters last-in, first-out and resume surviving parents without recasting, paying again, or replaying their earlier Refrain/Dissonance. Negation refunds no costs and restores no prior concentration. Countering one spell is not whole-Action/turn hard denial and does not spend that combined ledger.


## Reviewed placement-specific cards

Detect Poison has Divination rank-0 and Abjuration rank-1 modes. The casting class's preserved school/rank selects the mode; the rank-1 mode also requires F. Alignment Shield has Abjuration rank-1/30-foot and Conjuration rank-3/60-foot modes; its 60-foot header represents only the maximum range across modes. Read each full target and resolution field. These are manuscript rules; the pricing helper does not execute targeting or components.

Repulsion Field's operational entry is only the rank-1 object pulse. Its distinct rank-6 creature effect remains preserved but unavailable. Warding Bond uses its preserved rank-1 class access; the rank-2 duplicate grants no extra effect. Higher character level or extra RP never grants a blocked placement or changes modes. All source variants remain in the catalog's source evidence.

Alignment Sanctuary has Abjuration rank-3 admission saves and the actually granted Shaman Conjuration rank-6 matching-alignment mode. The unassigned rank-6 Abjuration benefits remain unavailable. Identity counts do not close every preserved placement; consult the [variant register](SPELL_VARIANT_REVIEW_STATUS.json).

Ordinary Warding Bond follows the reviewed damage-sharing stage/root rules and its exact card. It does not use or enlarge the Paladin class redirection round ledger or grant named Paladin healing/resource riders. Its authored promotion does not establish an implementation of its effect in the damage-sharing reference helper.

## Reviewed finite conjurations

## Falling bridge — new provisional procedure

This is a newly authored table procedure agreed with the GPT notebook, **not recovered V6/Core V2 canon**. Focused searches of the current rulebook extract, Core V2 and mechanics/manual text found spell summaries but no operational falling clock or impact formula. Before promotion to canon, inspect the approved V6 environment/travel/hazard sections and archived environment tables. Preserve any older rule found and compare it explicitly.

When a creature loses support with no movement mode or effect keeping it aloft, it enters **Falling** immediately. Falling means unsupported; it grants no hovering, airborne walking or lateral movement. Track total distance descended during this fall and cumulative distance during its current uncontrolled portion, both initially zero.

**Timing:** If a fall begins during a regular initiative turn, set a fixed Fall Marker at the **end of that initiative slot in the following round**. Resolve the first Falling Step there, then one at the same marker each round. Reactions and extra turns use the enclosing regular initiative slot; an event between slots uses the most recently completed slot. Extra turns, extra Actions and initiative changes neither move nor multiply the marker. This gives every participant one normal turn opportunity before the first descent; inability to act still matters and no free rescue action is granted. A caster still needs legal targets within range when spending their Action.

Outside initiative, when timing matters, establish an order before descent and use a virtual slot immediately before its first regular slot as the initiating slot. The first step occurs when that virtual slot next recurs, after everyone has had one normal turn opportunity. When no rescue or other timing decision is possible, the Director can resolve the same descent and impact calculation directly. This is an explicit timing abstraction, not a model of physical acceleration.

If a fall begins after initiative has been established but before any regular initiative slot has yet completed, treat the virtual pre-round slot as the most recently completed slot for Fall Marker purposes.

**Ordinary descent:** At each step descend up to **300 feet**, stopping on a supporting surface. Add the distance to both trackers. On landing while uncontrolled, take **min(10, floor(uncontrolled distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning damage**. The uncontrolled distance includes earlier steps; never use only the final step's remainder.

**Feather Fall:** The spell retains its **Action** casting time and reduces descent to at most **60 feet per step**. When it takes effect, set uncontrolled distance to zero: the magic dissipates prior uncontrolled momentum in this abstraction. Keep total fall distance. If landing while it remains active, damage is **min(3, floor(total fall distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning**. This explicitly limits impact exposure without guaranteeing a harmless landing. When the spell ends aloft, reset uncontrolled distance to zero, then accumulate ordinary descent from that point at the existing marker; expiry grants no immediate extra step. Its one-minute maximum ends immediately before the caster's regular turn ten rounds after casting. If expiry and a step coincide, resolve expiry first. Earlier landing or cessation of Falling ends the spell on that target as printed.

Apply damage defenses only when their actual wording covers that damage. After damage, Falling ends; a creature suffering any positive falling damage lands **Prone** unless an explicit feature prevents it. Less than 20 relevant feet produces zero damage. Forced movement that removes support starts a fall but adds no separate fall damage. Regaining genuine support, secure support from a hold, or flight ends Falling without resolving an uncompleted impact; teleporting safely onto support likewise ends it. A later loss of support begins a new fall with new trackers and marker. Completed impact and damage cannot be undone by later casting.

| Scenario | Steps to land | Impact |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ordinary 10 feet | 1 | 0 |
| Ordinary 20 feet | 1 | 1d6 |
| Ordinary 300 feet | 1 | 10d6 |
| Ordinary 310 feet | 2 | 10d6 |
| Ordinary 610 feet | 3 | 10d6 |
| Feather Fall active through a 310-foot fall | 6 | 3d6 |
| 120 feet slowed, spell ends aloft, then 190 feet uncontrolled | 3 | 9d6 |

The 300-foot ordinary step, impact formulas, momentum reset, marker and duration conventions are provisional inventions. The source supplies Feather Fall's Action, five targets and 60-foot slowed descent. Wider hazards, equipment catches, flight loss and environmental damage still need the combat/campaign pass.

Eight rank-two Evocation identities have [exact manuscript approval](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_EVOCATION_RANK2_EXACT_AND_DELIVERY_REVIEW.md). Their [complete cards](SPELL_PLAYTEST_STARTER.md) preserve five exact Core blocks and three separate possible historical-name blocks; matching metadata adoption does not merge identities or class access. Scorching Raystorm uses three independent attacks; line and burst spells keep their printed ranges. Shatter uses one fixed pre-damage snapshot and bounded structural sections. Frost Nova's specific elemental Speed 0 rider uses the existing refresh policy and reviewed Balanced Elements bridge. Acid Arrow's independently owned delayed packets keep their original one-shot markers and are not new casts. See [review status](EVOCATION_RANK2_REVIEW_STATUS.json) for remaining runtime and balance work.


## Reviewed ancestry spell access

The [ancestry/background integration](ANCESTRY_BACKGROUND_PLAYTEST.md) defines a separate explicit casting source for40 fixed grants and two Wizard-cantrip choices. These grants use their own total-level gates, ability, school/mode and recharge; they do not create ordinary class access, an RP pool or RC conversion. Charge-only casts retain actual components/actions/concentration/interruption and shared Dissonance/Refrain, have no RP-price interface, and remain blocked at their actual Limit+6 for ranked casting. The focus token is ancestry-scoped only. Read the guide for exact short/long-rest recovery, Oracle and Echo of the Stolen rules.

The [seventeen dependency procedures](ANCESTRY_SPELL_SUPPLEMENT_PLAYTEST.md) comprise seven existing IDs promoted into this ordinary catalog and ten separate ancestry-grant-only additions. The additions have no ordinary class access. The original848IDs/936placements remain intact; full ordinary spell mechanics, live runtime and human balance remain open.
